verdicts.strongest_argument: Three things put this well up the scale, and the hunter concedes the most important one. First, it is published in the corpus: the position change is reported in the stored Stocktwits body at the 2026-08-28T20:57:39Z entry (docs/9d6320246d8c47c15bc0b33e8312f82c2fb4986e.txt), so it was circulating in the retail stream six days before the print - the finding's own quote, 'while retail is running scared, institutions keep accumulating', is that circulation. Second, 13F holdings are a quarterly public dataset that dozens of free trackers parse and republish within hours of filing; a top-five holder doubling a position is exactly the change those services headline. Third, and decisively, the hunter states the disqualifying caveat itself: a 13F filed 2026-08-12 reports positions as of 30 June, so this is a fact about Q2 ownership disclosed six weeks late and says nothing about flow into the print - and the tape since then is -19.23% over twenty sessions and -13.28% over five, which is what it looks like when whoever owns the stock is not defending it. Ownership composition is also not a directional claim about a quarter's results; it changes who reacts, not what is reported. The small 9/18 call buyer noted as corroboration is one retail options observation with no size.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Baseline: spot 18.35, run_up_5d -13.28%, run_up_20d -19.23%, pct_from_52w_high -64.30%, pct_from_52w_low +184.06%, avg_volume_20d 6,490,910. The 8.6m-share position change is roughly 1.3 days of volume, and it was disclosed on 08-12 into a tape that has fallen 19% since. Median historical reaction 25.98% with a 49.37% maximum - this name's print risk is an order of magnitude larger than an ownership datapoint.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence of accumulation after 30 June - a 13G/A, a block print, a disclosed secondary purchase - which would turn stale ownership into live flow.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is an interpretation of the drawdown built from the drawdown, plus retail commentary that is itself in the capture. Every element is published in the same stored body - 'the volatility before spacex', 'the pumpers that disappeared after the spacex ipo', '10 of last 11 days red' - so the capital-rotation narrative is not missing from the observed corpus, it is the observed corpus. The RKLB lockstep is likewise computed from two public price series that anyone can overlay, and the SpaceX listing is one of the most heavily covered market events imaginable; a sector rotation into a newly listed giant is structural and known, not a hidden mechanism. The load-bearing inference - 'if the market were pricing a Planet-specific deterioration there would be a filing, a downgrade or a contract loss to point at, and the filing record is empty' - is an argument from the absence of evidence in a capture that contains no news search at all, which is precisely the reasoning the instructions rule out. Markets de-rate on estimate drift, macro and sector multiple compression without any of those three artefacts. And the 'unusually low volume' claim sits oddly against avg_volume_20d of 6.49m shares in a $7.5bn name. I also have to flag that the cited source URL for this finding is a European public-procurement notice (ted.europa.eu), which has no bearing on any assertion in it - the actual evidence is the Stocktwits body.
